h2: Water Pumps & Filters Canggu – Reliable Supply for Your Villa
intro: Canggu grew fast from rice fields into villas and co-living spaces, and the plumbing behind all that often shows its age within a couple of seasons. From pumps cycling non-stop in Berawa to brackish well water near the coast, I handle Water Pumps & Filters Canggu work so your supply stays steady through heavy rain and dry spells alike.

sections.h3: Why Canggu's Groundwater Makes Pump Work Tricky
sections.text: Former paddies keep the water table high across Canggu, feeding wells easily but also filling septic tanks faster and backing up drains after rain. Near Echo Beach, groundwater often carries a brackish tinge that corrodes pump seals and clogs filter media ahead of schedule. Up on the Bukit, most villas run off rooftop tanks supplied by those same wells, so one failed pressure switch can leave an entire property dry within minutes. Before recommending anything, I assess well output, tank capacity and line slope to find where the real bottleneck sits.

sections.h3: The Call-Outs I See Most Around Berawa
sections.text: A pump clicking on and off every few seconds usually points to a worn pressure switch or air trapped in the line—common in villas built quickly during Cangru's construction boom. Tank overflow is another frequent request: float valves seize in hard water and suddenly your ceiling is getting wet. Then there are the no-water mornings when a motor simply gives out after months of non-stop running. Filter cartridge swaps and full rooftop-tank cleanings round out my weekly list here. Each job gets a photo-based quote on WhatsApp before any work starts.

sections.h3: What to Send Me on WhatsApp for a Quick Quote
sections.text: You don't need to be a plumber to get a useful estimate. A short clip of the pump cycling, the tank gauge, or the filter housing tells me far more than a paragraph of description. Note where the unit lives—under-stairs pump room, rooftop platform, garden corner—and roughly when the issue started, and I can size up parts and access before arriving. Drop those photos or videos into our WhatsApp chat along with a line about what you'd like sorted, and I'll reply with a straightforward plan. Everything from quote to follow-up stays in that single conversation.

sections.h3: Small Habits That Save Your Pump Through Rainy Season
sections.text: Canggu's rainy season is hard on plumbing nobody has checked in months. Before October hits, test the pressure switch, free the float valve, and confirm the pump-room floor drains so no water reaches the wiring. Around Babakan, where former paddy soil still holds moisture, inspect the well screen for silt every six months—far cheaper than swapping a clogged motor. Rotate filter cartridges on schedule instead of waiting for flow to weaken, and glance at the rooftop tank after each heavy downpour. A few minutes of routine care keeps you out of the emergency queue when everyone else needs help at once.

faq.q: Is my well water too brackish for the villa?
faq.a: It depends on where your borehole sits relative to the coastline; I can test the output and recommend the right filtration setup if there's a salt or mineral load. Send a photo of any scale or discolouration over WhatsApp and I'll advise from there.

faq.q: How often should I clean the rooftop tank?
faq.a: In Canggu's humidity and dust levels, a visual check every three months and a full internal clean once a year keeps the supply safe and the float mechanism working properly. If you notice a change in taste or a pressure drop, message me sooner rather than later.

faq.q: My pump keeps turning on and off—what's usually wrong?
faq.a: Most often it's a worn pressure switch, air in the suction line, or a small upstream leak dropping system pressure below the cut-out point. A short video of the cycling sent over WhatsApp is enough for me to narrow down which one it is before I visit.
